query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended as energetic structural materials, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release? State the proposed intervention, its hypothesized mechanism, the improvement expected relative to the untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In the NbTiAlZrHfTaMoW refractory high‐entropy alloy, a controlled minor addition of a ductility‐promoting element (e.g., a slight increase of the Hf content by 1–2 at.%) will refine and uniformize the distribution of antiphase domain boundaries and stimulate more homogeneous dislocation slip activation, resulting in improved ductility and uniform deformability without a loss in high specific yield strength or impact-induced energy release.
generation.material_initial_state: NbTiAlZrHfTaMoW RHEA processed to yield a B2 matrix with antiphase domains, as previously reported.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled, low-level (approximately 1–2 at.%) increase in a ductile alloying element (for example, Hf) into the alloy’s composition.
generation.conditions: The intervention is expected to be effective at room temperature and elevated conditions (e.g., 1023–1123 K) under quasi-static and dynamic high-strain-rate impact loading relevant to energetic structural applications.
generation.structural_mediator: A more uniform and refined network of antiphase domain boundaries and associated dislocation slip bands resulting from the modified local chemistry.
generation.mechanism: The added ductile element is hypothesized to locally alter bonding and solid solution interactions, which encourages the formation of a more homogeneously distributed network of slip bands and domain boundaries. This in turn facilitates dynamic recovery and uniform plastic deformation while preserving the strong solid solution strengthening essential for high yield strength and energy release upon impact.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the untreated baseline alloy, the doped material will exhibit increased ductility (greater homogeneous strain before failure) and more uniformly distributed plastic deformation while maintaining similar high specific yield strength and impact-induced energy release characteristics.
generation.baseline: The as-synthesized NbTiAlZrHfTaMoW RHEA without the additional ductile element adjustment.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are expected only within a narrow dopant concentration window (around 1–2 at.%); higher additions may lead to coarsening or aggregation adverse to strength or energy release. The hypothesis applies to alloys with an established B2 matrix and antiphase domain structure.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative improvements and the optimum dopant concentration require further experimental validation, and the precise balance between ductility enhancement and retention of high strength/energy release remains to be defined.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a set of NbTiAlZrHfTaMoW alloy samples with systematically varied Hf additions (e.g., 0, 1, 2, and 3 at.% extra Hf). Characterize their microstructures using TEM and SEM to quantify the distribution and morphology of antiphase domains and dislocation slip bands. Conduct room temperature and high-temperature compression tests as well as high-strain-rate impact tests to measure ductility, specific yield strength, and energy release (via deflagration or related dynamic indicators).
measurements: Quantitative assessment of antiphase domain boundary uniformity (via TEM image analysis)
Stress–strain curves under quasi-static and dynamic loading
Measurement of fracture strain (ductility) and yield strength
Dynamic energy release parameters (e.g., peak pressure, release rates) under impact testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples with 1–2 at.% Hf addition fail to show a statistically significant improvement in uniform plastic deformation (as evidenced by more uniform slip band distribution and increased fracture strain) without any reduction in yield strength or impact-induced energy release compared to the baseline composition, then the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractThe NbTiAlZrHfTaMoW refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) system with the structure of the B2 matrix (antiphase domains) and antiphase domain boundaries was firstly developed. We conducted the mechanical properties of the RHEAs at 298 K, 1023 K, 1123 K, and 1223 K, as well as typical deformation characteristics. The RHEAs with low density (7.41~7.51 g/cm3) have excellent compressive-specific yield strength (σYS/ρ) at 1023 K (~131 MPa·cm3/g) and 1123 K (~104.2 MPa·cm3/g), respectively, which are far superior to most typical RHEAs. And, they still keep appropriate plastic deformability at room temperature (ε > 0.35). The superior specific yield strengths are mainly attributed to the solid solution strengthening induced by the Zr element. The formation of the dislocation slip bands with [111](101_) and [111](112_) directions and their interaction provide considerable plastic deformation capability. Meanwhile, dynamic recrystallization and dislocation annihilation accelerate the continuous softening after yielding at 1123 K.Keywords: refractory high-entropy alloys, B2 phase, specific yield strength, strain softening, deformation microstructure

## Abstract
AbstractHigh-energy structural materials (ESMs) integrate a high energy density with rapid energy release, offering promising applications in advanced technologies. In this study, a novel dual-phase Ti40Zr40W10Mo10 high-entropy alloy (HEA) was synthesized and evaluated as a potential ESM. The alloy exhibited a body-centered cubic (BCC) matrix with Mo-W-rich BCC precipitates of varying sizes, which increased proportionally with the W content. The compressive mechanical properties were assessed across a range of strain rates, revealing that the W10 HEA sustained a compressive strength of 2300 MPa at a strain rate of 3000 s−1. This exceptional performance is attributed to the uniform distribution of circular Mo-W-rich BCC precipitates. Conversely, in the W13 HEA, the aggregated and large Mo-W-rich precipitates deteriorated its dynamic properties. Furthermore, deflagration behavior was observed during dynamic deformation of W10, highlighting its potential as a high-performance ESM.Keywords: energetic structural materials, high-entropy alloys, microstructures, mechanical properties
